description: Establish the single source-of-truth PostgreSQL schema with Drizzle ORM + drizzle-kit in web/, replace the web/src/lib/db.ts file layer with a Drizzle-backed async data layer, migrate ALL web storage call sites, preserve the audit hash chain EXACTLY, rewrite the web test harness to be DB-backed, and rework Docker/seed infra (postgres service + migrate/seed replacing init-data). This FEAT creates the tables that FEAT-002 (scraper) maps to, so it comes first. Independent of FEAT-002's internals but FEAT-002 depends on the schema and seed produced here.
steps: Add dependencies to web/package.json: drizzle-orm, a Postgres driver (postgres or pg), and devDeps drizzle-kit (+ @types/pg if using pg). Add a `test` script (`jest`), `db:generate` (drizzle-kit generate), `db:migrate` (apply migrations), and `db:seed` scripts. Run `cd web && npm install` so package-lock.json is regenerated; commit it.

Create web/src/lib/schema.ts as the SINGLE source of truth: Drizzle pgTable definitions for users (text PK id, email, passwordHash, name, tier, maskedInbox, onboarded, 8 consent boolean columns matching ConsentFlags, createdAt), insurers (text PK, name, agentEmail, logo, persona, website), plans (text PK, insurerId FK, insurerName, planName, category, coverageAmount, premiums jsonb, premiumFrequency, coverageTerms jsonb/text[], illnessesCovered, earlyStageConditions, payoutType, keyBenefits jsonb, exclusions jsonb, sourceUrl, dataAsOf, updatedBadge, changeNotes jsonb, version, scrapedAt), sources (text PK, insurerId FK, label, url, type, planIds jsonb, etag, lastModified, contentHash, lastChecked, lastChanged, status), threads (text PK, userId FK, insurerId FK, insurerName, subject, status, extractedQuote jsonb nullable, riskFlags jsonb, addedToComparison, createdAt, updatedAt), thread_messages (text PK, threadId FK, ordering column, direction, from, to, subject, body, timestamp, aiGenerated, flagged, flagReason), scraper_runs (text PK runId, trigger, startedAt, finishedAt, sourcesChecked, sourcesChanged, errors jsonb), and audit_entries. Use snake_case column names with Drizzle field aliases to the camelCase names in web/src/lib/types.ts. Keep text PKs (ids like 'aia', 'user_demo'). Field names/types must match web/src/lib/types.ts exactly.

CRITICAL audit table design (web/src/lib/schema.ts audit_entries): columns = bigserial `id` (monotonic ordering, PRIMARY KEY), timestamp (text — store the exact ISO string, NOT timestamptz), actor (text), action (text), detail (text — store the raw JSON string, NOT jsonb), prevHash (text), hash (text). Rationale recorded in code comment: jsonb reorders keys and renormalizes whitespace/numbers, which breaks sha256(JSON.stringify(partial)). Storing detail as the exact serialized text and timestamp as text guarantees byte-identical recomputation.

Create web/src/lib/db.ts replacement (keep the same module path so imports are stable): export an async Drizzle data layer. Provide async query helpers that the call sites need (e.g. getUsers/getUserById/updateUser, getInsurers/getInsurerById, getPlans, getThreadsByUser/getThreadById/insertThread/appendThreadMessage/updateThread, getScraperRuns, and audit insert/read). Initialize the Drizzle client from process.env.DATABASE_URL. Do NOT import this into edge code (auth.config.ts/middleware).

Rewrite web/src/lib/audit.ts to use the DB: logEvent reads the last audit row by `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1` for prevHash (else '0'), builds `partial` with EXACT key order timestamp,actor,action,detail,prevHash, computes hash=sha256(JSON.stringify(partial)), and inserts a row storing timestamp (ISO text), actor, action, detail=JSON.stringify(partial.detail) (exact text), prevHash, hash. verifyChain reads ALL rows ORDER BY id ASC, rebuilds the partial object IN THE SAME KEY ORDER using the stored detail TEXT (parse only if needed, but hash over the stored text to guarantee fidelity), recomputes, and returns {valid, entries, brokenAt?}. logEvent and verifyChain become async. Preserve the '0' first-prevHash and brokenAt index semantics.

Update every web call site to the async data layer with `await`: web/src/lib/auth.ts (authorize user lookup), web/src/lib/mail.ts (daily-limit + follow-up-cooldown thread reads; sendEmail already async), web/src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts (await logEvent + user update), web/src/app/api/outreach/send/route.ts (insurers/users/threads + create/append thread), web/src/app/api/outreach/draft/route.ts, web/src/app/api/plans/route.ts, web/src/app/api/insurers/route.ts, web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts, web/src/app/api/crm/threads/route.ts, web/src/app/api/crm/threads/[threadId]/route.ts, web/src/app/api/crm/threads/[threadId]/quote/route.ts (await logEvent), web/src/app/api/scraper/status/route.ts. Preserve all existing filtering/sorting/auth/policy behavior. Keep `export const dynamic` and `await params` conventions.

Add drizzle.config.ts in web/ pointing at schema.ts, out dir web/drizzle, dialect postgresql, DATABASE_URL from env. Run `cd web && npm run db:generate` to produce the SQL migration + journal; commit the generated web/drizzle/* files.

Create a seed loader (web/src/lib/seed.ts or a script invoked by db:seed) that reads seed/*.json and inserts rows into the DB in FK-safe order (insurers, users, plans, sources, threads + messages), leaving audit_entries and scraper_runs empty. This becomes the DB equivalent of the old JSON seed.

Rewrite the web test harness: web/src/__tests__/setup.ts must set up a test database (point DATABASE_URL at a disposable test DB, run migrations, load seed) instead of copying JSON to a temp DATA_DIR. web/src/__tests__/audit.test.ts must 'tamper' by mutating an audit_entries ROW (e.g. UPDATE action) instead of editing a file line, asserting the SAME verifyChain outcomes (valid true for clean chain of 3, valid false with brokenAt 0 after tamper, valid true for empty). Keep policy.test.ts and blocker.test.ts passing (they do not touch storage — verify).

Rework infra: docker-compose.yml — add a `postgres` service (with healthcheck) and a DATABASE_URL env for both `web` and `scraper`; replace the init-data JSON-copy service with a migrate+seed step (new one-shot service or entrypoint running db:migrate then db:seed) that web/scraper depend on via service_completed_successfully/healthy. LEAVE the scraper LLM config (HERMES_API_KEY, Anthropic LLM_MODEL), Mailpit, WEB_BASE_URL, SCRAPER_URL untouched. Add DATABASE_URL to .env.example, web/.env.local.example. Keep DATA_DIR_OVERRIDE only if still needed for versions/ snapshots.

Rewrite seed/reset.sh so `./dev.sh seed` resets the DATABASE to seed state (truncate tables + reload seed, or drop/recreate schema via drizzle then seed) instead of copying JSON. Keep ./dev.sh seed/test/up command surface working. data/versions/<sourceId>/*.html stays on filesystem.
Append a TASK.MD entry per the CLAUDE.md protocol summarizing the web+schema+infra migration and noting that FEAT-002 (scraper SQLAlchemy mapping) depends on this schema.
acceptance_criteria: `cd web && npm install` succeeds and package-lock.json is updated with drizzle-orm, the Postgres driver, and drizzle-kit.
`cd web && npm run build` compiles with no type errors; `cd web && npm run lint` passes.

`cd web && npm test` passes, including the rewritten DB-backed audit.test.ts: clean 3-entry chain verifies valid; a tampered row yields valid=false with brokenAt=0; empty chain is valid with entries=0. policy.test.ts and blocker.test.ts still pass.
Drizzle migration files exist under web/drizzle and are committed; applying them to an empty Postgres creates all tables.
db:seed loads the 5 insurers, demo user, plans, sources with text PKs matching seed/*.json.
No web source file imports fs-based readJSON/writeJSON/appendJSONL/readJSONL/dataFileExists anymore (the old file layer is gone); a grep for those old fs bodies returns only historical/none.
docker-compose.yml defines a postgres service and DATABASE_URL for web and scraper; the JSON-copy init-data step is replaced by a migrate+seed step; scraper LLM/Mailpit env is unchanged.
verification: cd web && npm run db:generate (confirm migration files are produced/committed) and apply migrations + db:seed against a disposable Postgres to confirm schema + seed load
